item.title: Morning Digest, Thursday 12 November 2026
item.description:
Nvidia's board reportedly prepares to remove Jensen Huang, Russia and Ukraine agree a large prisoner swap, Iran says Hormuz stays shut, the Tidö parties overtake the left in a new poll, and Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to paying developers.

Today's must-read

A Strange Quantum Theorem Has Killed Einstein’s Reality (Quanta Magazine (Charlie Wood))

Traces the argument over whether the quantum state describes reality itself or only our knowledge of it, from Einstein's 1935 objection and Bell's 1964 theorem to the 2012 PBR theorem, which rules out the comfortable middle ground in which the wavefunction is mere information about an objective world. Recent tests, including one run on an IBM quantum computer, back the theorem, leaving physicists to choose between a strange objective reality and none at all. A clear 'aha' about what quantum mechanics actually forbids, told through the people who proved it.

Everyone's talking about

Nvidia's board reportedly moves to oust Jensen Huang

The Wall Street Journal reports the board is preparing to remove Nvidia's co-founder and only chief executive in 33 years, after the New York Times reported a second affair, this one with a vice-president who reports directly to him; nothing is final, and finance chief Colette Kress is named as a possible interim CEO. Shares fell about 8 percent after hours on Wednesday, on top of more than 450 billion dollars in lost market value since the board opened its inquiry on 8 November.

WSJ via CBS News; Tom's Hardware; NYT, 11 Nov

Abu Dhabi talks end with a deal on a large prisoner swap

After two days of US-mediated talks, the first direct ones since February, Russia and Ukraine agreed a large exchange of prisoners of war; Kushner says the numbers will be fixed today, and TASS expects the swap within two to three weeks. Territory, which Kushner called the hardest issue, did not move. He and Witkoff now go to Moscow to brief Putin and then to Dublin to see Zelensky, whose team wants Europe in the next round.

Al Jazeera; AP via Just Security, 11 Nov

Iran says Hormuz stays shut as Trump predicts a quick end

Trump said on Wednesday that the war would end soon. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei denied any talks with Washington, set seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, starting with an end to fighting on all fronts including Lebanon, and warned that a new US attack would bring strikes on US bases in Europe. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved onto a military base because of Iranian threats, the New York Times reports.

Iran International; Just Security (NYT, Reuters), 11 Nov

World

UK arrests a US soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia

Counter-terrorism police arrested a 41-year-old senior US Army soldier near Gloucester on Tuesday under the National Security Act, with MI5 and the FBI involved. It came a day after US tanker planes left RAF Mildenhall over an Iranian threat.

Times of Israel; BBC via Just Security, 10-11 Nov

House report finds no evidence against Trump in Epstein cases

The Republican-led Oversight Committee concluded that federal authorities mishandled the Epstein investigations but found nothing implicating Trump, and called Democratic claims unfounded.

NPR via Just Security, 11 Nov

Sweden

The left meets again as the polls turn

The four red-green parties met on Wednesday for the first time since Monday's talks collapsed and called it constructive, but Left Party leader Nooshi Dadgostar says V still demands cabinet seats, and Magdalena Andersson asked the Speaker to wait one to two weeks before the next prime-minister vote. The Centre Party repeats it will back no government with SD or V. An SVT/Verian poll puts S at 26.1 percent, its lowest under Andersson, and the Tidö parties ahead of the red-greens for the first time in over four years, 50.6 to 47.7 percent, within the margin of error.

SVT; Corren (TT); Pressen, 11 Nov

The Riksdag opens the door to revoking citizenship

Parliament passed for the second and final time a constitutional change that allows citizenship to be withdrawn if it was obtained with false information, or after convictions for crimes that seriously harm Sweden's vital interests. It takes effect on 1 January 2027, but a separate law must still list the crimes and decide whether existing citizenships are covered.

Verifiera; Sveriges Radio, 11 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government's 2027 budget at 08:00, Riksdag debate from 13:00; Sweden's extended border checks begin; European Political Community summit in Dublin; UK third-quarter GDP; prisoner-swap numbers due from the Abu Dhabi talks.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's 17:00 deadline for S and M to present full government plans; informal EU leaders' summit in Dublin; Mississippi certifies its Senate result.
  • Tuesday 17 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker on government formation.
  • Later next week: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; Anthropic expected to start trading on Nasdaq on 19 November.

Riksdagen; Regeringen; Rio Times; Al Jazeera; CNBC; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to paying users

Two weeks after a restricted launch for cyber defenders, Google's top model is on the paid Gemini API, Google AI Ultra and GitHub Copilot at 2 dollars per million input tokens and 10 per million output, doubling after an introductory period. It scores 60 on Artificial Analysis's independent index, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65; Google also previewed /swarm, which splits one coding task across parallel agents checked by adversarial reviewer agents.

Google; Data Studios; Mad Robot, 10 Nov

Alibaba previews Qwen4-Max

The first model of the next Qwen generation reads images and video, handles up to a million tokens of context and is available through Alibaba's Token Plan subscription and Qwen apps. Alibaba gave no benchmarks and has not said whether weights will be released.

TechNode; Qwen, 11 Nov

MiniMax releases an open-weight image model

The Shanghai lab's H3-Image generates and edits pictures from up to 16 reference images and, by its own claim, renders 4K images in under ten seconds; the weights are downloadable.

MiniMax via The Neuron, 10 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Tree-Ising (QDeep, ITMO University): recasts a recent agent-written weight repair of a looping Qwen3.5-0.8B as one small Ising optimisation per weight row; it beats the GPT-6 Astra agent's fix on MATH-500 (54.6 against 51.7 percent) with fewer changed weights and about 0.90 dollars of compute instead of 312, though the recipe was designed after studying the agent's logs (arXiv 2611.14210, top of Hugging Face papers).
  • WikiTrace (KAIST): agent memory that links each distilled lesson back to the run it came from so the agent can check it before acting; across eight benchmark suites it averages 90.2 against 79.5 without memory and cuts the cases where memory makes an agent fail tasks it would otherwise solve (arXiv 2611.14320, Hugging Face and alphaXiv).
  • Evolving Infra (Georgia Tech, UIUC, Berkeley, MIT and others): a serving system that moves GPUs between reading prompts and generating text as agent workloads shift, and keeps the cached context agents will reuse; on real Claude Code traces it cuts mean latency up to 4.1 times against Nvidia's Dynamo (arXiv 2611.12304, alphaXiv trending).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face, 9-10 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Wednesday 11 November 2026
item.description:
House Republicans bury the Hegseth impeachment and pick Jim Jordan as their leader, the Abu Dhabi talks turn to a large prisoner swap, Anthropic prices its IPO at up to 1.4 trillion dollars, Sweden's government question could be settled within ten days, and DeepMind's AI proves Signal's encryption code does what it promises.

Everyone's talking about

House Republicans kill the Hegseth impeachment and choose Jordan to lead them

The House voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send Thomas Massie's eight articles against the defence secretary to the Judiciary Committee, which ends the effort in this Congress; Massie was the only Republican against. The same day, Republicans picked Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise, 106 to 73, to lead them in the minority when Democrats take the House in January.

ABC News; Democracy Now, 10 Nov

Abu Dhabi talks focus on a large prisoner swap

Russia, Ukraine and the US met for nearly four hours, with Kushner and Witkoff mediating and Budanov on Ukraine's team. Zelensky said the talks were mostly humanitarian (prisoners, detained civilians, deported children), with details of a large exchange to follow; on territory the sides remain far apart. Europeans joined a coordination meeting beforehand but not the three-way session, which Russia opposed. Day two is today.

AP via Boston Globe; Euronews, 10 Nov

Anthropic sets its IPO range at 70-78 dollars a share

Selling 825 million shares would raise up to 64 billion dollars and value the company at up to 1.4 trillion, below the 2 trillion floated weeks ago amid an AI share sell-off; seven partners including Google and Nvidia will buy a further 26 billion dollars of non-voting stock. Trading on Nasdaq as ANT could start on 19 November, sources told CNBC.

Fortune; CNBC, 10 Nov

World

Merz ties the EU budget to Ukraine

Germany's chancellor threatens to block the EU's next seven-year budget unless all 27 members commit to funding Ukraine after 2027, when Kyiv faces a gap of about 70 billion euros. Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia stayed out of the current 90-billion-euro loan, and Bulgaria says it won't add more; Council president Costa tried to reassure Berlin.

Euronews, 10 Nov

US prices rose 0.4 percent in October

Core prices, which leave out volatile food and energy, rose 0.3 percent, above forecasts; Bloomberg says this supports a Federal Reserve rate rise. The usual annual rate is missing because last year's shutdown stopped October 2025 data collection.

BLS; Bloomberg, 10 Nov

US tankers leave a second British base

American refuelling planes left RAF Mildenhall on Monday over an alleged Iranian threat, the Wall Street Journal reports, a month after B-1 bombers left RAF Fairford.

WSJ via Democracy Now, 10 Nov

Sweden

The government question could be settled next week

Speaker Andreas Norlén says Ulf Kristersson will report on his exploratory mission on Tuesday 17 November, after which Norlén will consult the other parties; SVT's Mats Knutson expects a prime-minister vote could follow late next week. The Centre Party is negotiating with both S and M and wants each to present a full governing plan by Friday at 17:00. On the left, the Left Party has agreed to resume talks with S, C and the Greens, according to sources cited by SVT, and LO is urging it to drop its demand for cabinet seats.

Riksdagen; SVT; Altinget, 6-10 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Wednesday 11 November: second day of US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi; COP31 leaders' summit in Antalya (to Thursday); the Riksdag's final vote on stripping some dual citizens of Swedish citizenship.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government's 2027 budget at 08:00, Riksdag debate from 13:00; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's 17:00 deadline for S and M to present full government plans; informal EU leaders' summit in Dublin; Mississippi certifies its Senate result, where Democrat Scott Colom leads.
  • Tuesday 17 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker on government formation.
  • Later next week: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; Anthropic expected to start trading on Nasdaq on 19 November.

Riksdagen; Altinget; Regeringen; Democracy Now; CNBC; earlier editions

Tech and AI

DeepMind's AI proves Signal's encryption code keeps its promises

AlphaProof Code, a system of Gemini-powered agents, wrote over six million lines of Lean proofs showing that libsignal, the core of Signal's messaging protocol, delivers forward secrecy and authentication down to the compiled machine code. A team of five did it in four weeks and only about 1 percent of the code was flagged for human review; the proofs assume the underlying cryptography is perfect and do not cover the whole app.

Google DeepMind; Qodo; Unite.AI, 10 Nov

Claude designs working gadgets from short prompts

Anthropic and hardware startup Diode Computers had Fable 5.2 produce schematics, circuit boards, cases and firmware for a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub and a handheld virtual pet; Diode built all three from Claude's files and they worked without circuit fixes. They are early prototypes without safety or electrical certification.

Anthropic, 9 Nov

OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly near 10 billion dollars

Bloomberg reports third-quarter revenue rose nearly 50 percent to about 10 billion dollars; OpenAI has not published the figure.

Bloomberg, 10 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Embodied First Exam (Northwestern, CMU, Berkeley, Stanford and others): 1,156 robot tasks for coding agents that may control, script or train a robot; GPT-6 Astra solves 30 percent of core tasks through sensors alone but 77 percent with full simulator access and free resets, which shows that undoing mistakes matters more than perfect state information (arXiv 2611.12177, alphaXiv trending).
  • LingBot-Touch (Robbyant): one tactile encoder trained on 5,000 hours of glove and robot-hand data from three sensor types works on an unseen sensor without retraining and lifts success on 26 real two-arm tasks by 14-26 points across four policy families, while raw touch signals give at most half that (arXiv 2611.12806, top of Hugging Face papers).
  • Agency (UC Berkeley, Ion Stoica's group): harness choice barely changes coding-agent accuracy but can double cost; re-reading accumulated context is up to 73 percent of spend, and transparent fixes such as pruning finished subtasks and indexing files cut cost by 23 percent on average with Claude Code and Codex (arXiv 2611.12122, alphaXiv).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face, 9-10 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Tuesday 10 November 2026
item.description:
Trump calls the Iran war militarily over but keeps the blockade, Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi with Europe at the table, Trump disputes the midterms as the House moves on Hegseth, Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 days before its listing, and Merz picks Ilse Aigner to be Germany's first woman president.

Today's must-read

Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026 (METR)

The first outside audit of whether a frontier lab is using its own AI to speed up AI research. With staff interviews, surveys and Anthropic's internal benchmark index, METR estimates Anthropic now improves its models on well-specified tasks about twice as fast as in 2024-25 (plausibly 1.3x to 3x), finds that training compute growth did not accelerate, and judges that about 80 percent of the speed-up comes from AI itself. It is also candid about the limits: Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative. A first-hand look at the mechanics behind the 'recursive self-improvement' talking point.

Everyone's talking about

Trump says the Iran war is 'effectively over', but the blockade stays

After meeting Qatar's prime minister, who brought a two-day Iranian proposal, Trump said the war is over militarily and he expects it to end 'fairly soon', while the naval blockade and the new land-and-Caspian task force remain. Iranian officials called his remarks fake news; President Pezeshkian said Iran will negotiate but not yield to force, and still demands sanctions relief, frozen funds and an end to Israel's strikes in Lebanon.

Al Jazeera, 9 Nov

Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi, with Europe in the room

The first US-Russia-Ukraine round since February runs today and tomorrow, with Witkoff and Kushner hosting Umerov's and Medinsky's delegations. For the first time the EU sends its own team, led by von der Leyen's and Costa's top aides, alongside France, Germany and the UK; Brussels wants Black Sea shipping restored and a ceasefire on energy and food infrastructure.

Euronews, 9 Nov

Trump disputes the midterms as the House moves to impeach Hegseth

Days after accepting the results, Trump asked on Truth Social whether anyone believed the election was honest, offering no evidence. Separately, Thomas Massie filed eight impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth on Monday, which forces a House vote within two legislative days; Trump says he will stand by Hegseth.

Al Jazeera; CBS News; CNN, 9 Nov

Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of its listing

Fable 5.2 is 20 percent cheaper than 5.1 (8 and 40 dollars per million input and output tokens) and beats Anthropic's Opus 5.5 on its coding, computer-use and research benchmarks, all company-reported. Mythos 5.2 is the same model with looser cyber and biology safeguards, still limited to vetted organisations; Anthropic also says the model solved two open problems on black holes in holographic duality, which outsiders have not yet checked.

Anthropic; The Next Web, 9 Nov

World

Merz nominates Ilse Aigner for German president

The CSU speaker of Bavaria's parliament, backed by the CDU, CSU and the SPD's leader, is expected to win the Federal Convention vote on 30 January and would be Germany's first female head of state.

Xinhua; ZDF, 6-9 Nov

Netanyahu offers a unity government as the new Knesset is sworn in

A day after losing the mandate to Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu argued Likud should lead as the largest party. Eisenkot and Liberman have agreed on a speaker, but Liberman still rules out depending on the Arab-led parties, which Eisenkot's 67-seat majority needs.

Open Magazine; Jerusalem Post, 9-10 Nov

Amsterdam's biggest Gaza march

Organisers including Amnesty counted over 200,000 people on Sunday demanding an end to Dutch arms trade with Israel and wider sanctions; Prime Minister Jetten, who marched last year, stayed away. Police gave no estimate.

Al Jazeera, 8 Nov

Sweden

Sweden gets its first caretaker budget since 2019 on Thursday

With no new government, Svantesson will present a 2027 budget that rolls over this year's spending levels, adjusted for prices and existing law, and continues the defence build-up. Temporary measures lapse unless all eight parties agree, so fuel taxes and young people's payroll taxes would rise automatically. Parties can file rival budgets until 27 November, and the Riksdag decides on 9 December; a new government would amend it.

Regeringen; TV4, Oct-Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Tuesday 10 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi (to Wednesday); Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; US October inflation figures at 14:30; strike day in French schools and universities.
  • Wednesday 11 November: COP31 leaders' summit in Antalya (to Thursday); the Riksdag's final vote on stripping some dual citizens of Swedish citizenship; the House vote on impeaching Hegseth is due around midweek.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government's 2027 budget at 08:00, Riksdag debate from 13:00; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's deadline for M and S to present full government plans; informal EU leaders' summit in Dublin; French public-sector unions meet the government.
  • Next week: Anthropic aims to list on Nasdaq as ANT in the week of 16 November; APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, where Trump expects to see Xi and Putin.

Euronews; Jerusalem Post; Regeringen; Council of the EU; FinanceFeeds; Shenzhen government; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Nvidia falls 4 percent over the Huang affair

Shares dropped on Monday as the board's outside inquiry into the chief executive's relationship with a suspected Chinese agent began, and shareholders filed a class action seeking damages.

Yahoo Finance; SBS, 9-10 Nov

Meta's Muse Ember targets cheap agent work

Meta's smallest model costs 0.10 and 0.50 dollars per million input and output tokens, takes a million tokens of context, and scores 36 on Artificial Analysis's index, level with Claude Haiku 5.5 at about a third of the cost per task, though it trails Haiku on real coding tasks.

The Decoder; Meta, 9 Nov

Google adds two eighth-generation TPUs

TPU 8tx keeps data and model weights encrypted while they are processed, so firms can fine-tune and serve models on sensitive data; TPU 8i Max puts two inference chips in one package, doubling compute and memory bandwidth for very long contexts. Google gave no prices or ship dates.

Google, 9 Nov

Gemini can pull mail and Drive files into chats unasked

A user's documented tests show consumer Gemini with connected apps sometimes reads Gmail and Drive content without being asked; Google's terms say such content can reach human reviewers. The behaviour varies between runs and Google has not commented on the tests.

GitHub write-up; StartupHub.ai, 9-10 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • FinDendro (The Fin AI, Manchester, Florida): 2,226 dated US market facts show models know more than they admit; GPT-5 recalls 76 percent but claims to know 38, and telling it to answer 'as of' a past date removes the claims but not the knowledge, so backtests inside a model's training window can't be trusted (arXiv 2611.06808, Hugging Face papers).
  • FlashState (Together AI, UIUC, UT Austin): hybrid models that mix attention with recurrent layers are hard to cache for coding agents, which resend long shared prefixes; saving recurrent state at arbitrary positions gives up to 3.1 times vLLM's prefill throughput on GLM-5.3-Flash (alphaXiv, trending).
  • Hugging Face's MoE handbook: a free, 70,000-word guide from about 800,000 GPU hours of internal mixture-of-experts runs, covering expert sizing, router design, hiding communication cost and converting dense checkpoints, high on alphaXiv this week.

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face, 4-9 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Monday 9 November 2026
item.description:
Nvidia's board investigates Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese agent, a far-right gunman kills six in Kraków, Andersson proposes a red-green government without the Left Party and is immediately rebuffed, the House prepares to impeach Hegseth, and COP31 opens in Turkey.

Everyone's talking about

Jensen Huang admits an affair; Nvidia's board opens an inquiry

Nvidia's chief executive told staff he had been unfaithful to his wife after reports that US intelligence suspects the woman, a former executive at Singapore's Megaspeed, of working for China's Ministry of State Security to obtain restricted AI chips. Independent directors will run an outside investigation; the board sees no sign that secrets were compromised and still backs Huang. Beijing calls the spying claims baseless.

Tom's Hardware; The Week, citing the New York Times, 8-9 Nov

Far-right gunman kills six in Kraków's main square

A 25-year-old Pole in military-style clothing fired from his car into the crowded Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon, killing six and wounding at least 15, including two police officers; his parents and sister were later found dead at home. The interior minister calls it terrorism and says the suspect, shot and arrested by police, held ultra-nationalist views.

CBS News; NBC News; SVT Text, 7-8 Nov

Andersson proposes S, C and MP; the Left Party says no within hours

On Sunday Andersson proposed a Social Democrat, Centre and Green government, offering the Left Party influence through officials and joint policy work instead of ministers, and said S would go into full opposition against an M-KD-L-C government resting on SD. V's deputy leader replied that its congress requires cabinet seats and that V would vote against Andersson. The Centre Party awaits both blocs' full plans, due Friday; SVT's analyst says the stand-off now favours Kristersson or a snap election.

SVT, 8 Nov

House set to impeach Hegseth this week

Thomas Massie is reintroducing his eight-article resolution, including a charge that the Iran war broke the War Powers Act, and the House must vote within two legislative days; with a 218-214 split, four Republican defections would be enough to pass it. Conviction needs 67 senators, so removal is unlikely.

SBS; Inquisitr citing Axios, 8 Nov

Trump ties new Iran strikes to a deal; blockade extends to land

Trump told CNN fresh attacks are 'highly unlikely' if Iran signs a strong agreement, while a new US task force will police weapons, cash and sanctioned goods crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian. Iran demands seven US steps first, including sanctions relief and reparations.

Daily Maverick (Reuters); Fox News, 8 Nov

COP31 opens in Antalya with lower ambitions

The UN climate talks run to 20 November under a Turkish presidency, with Australia leading negotiations. National plans now add up to emissions only about 6 percent below 2019 by 2035, and 77 leaders are due at the summit on 11-12 November, against 116 at COP28.

Climate & Capital Media, 8 Nov

World

Europe rejects a US-Russia deal on its security

After meeting Putin's envoy Dmitriev, Trump spoke of a 'big agreement' with Moscow that 'might involve all of Europe'. Kaja Kallas replied that Putin has no veto over European security and the EU must be at the table; Poland's Sikorski called a deal about Europe without Europe impossible.

Türkiye Today; Euronews, 7 Nov

Hacked Russian records point to 394,000-450,000 war dead

Two hacker groups say death certificates taken from Russia's statistics agency show at least 393,881 deaths explicitly linked to the war through August, far above the 285,881 named by independent researchers. Rosstat admits an attack but denies any leak; the figures are unverified.

Kyiv Independent, 7 Nov

Saudi-Houthi war escalates

Saudi Arabia says it shot down three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province, and debris damaged an Aramco office building; Houthi health officials say Saudi-led strikes killed 33 near Sanaa. The 2022 truce collapsed in July.

Al Jazeera; Reuters, 8 Nov

Sweden

19-year-old charged over IS-inspired school attack plan

Prosecutors say he planned a knife attack on a high school in Halmstad this spring in the name of Islamic State; he is charged with membership of a terrorist organisation and public incitement, and the trial opens on 19 November.

The Local (AFP), 8 Nov

Stockholm VC

Funding

  • Green Voltis (CEO and co-founder Martin Kievit) — AI trading and control software that runs battery storage and renewable assets on European power markets, plus a plan to pair data centres with flexible energy — 13.5 million euros Series A — Lochpine Capital as sole investor.

ArcticStartup, 6 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Monday 9 November: COP31 opens in Antalya (to 20 November); Stephen Miller starts as White House chief of staff; the House returns and Massie reintroduces the Hegseth impeachment resolution; Lecornu meets French unions and employers on wages.
  • Tuesday 10 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi (to Wednesday); Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; US October inflation figures; national strike day in France.
  • Wednesday 11 November: COP31 leaders' summit (to Thursday); the Riksdag holds its second, final vote on allowing some dual citizens to be stripped of Swedish citizenship.
  • Thursday 12 November: deadline for the budget bill, so the caretaker government is expected to present a transitional budget; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's deadline for M and S to present full government plans; JPMorgan reportedly holds an investor session for Anthropic's planned listing.

Climate & Capital Media; SBS; Connexion; The Local; SVT; earlier editions

Tech and AI

DeepMind's agents find two weaknesses in legacy RSA-1024

Working with cryptographers Nadia Heninger and Emmanuel Thomé, AI agents produced a signature-forgery method estimated at about 1,600 times better than the best known approach in some cases, and a batch algorithm that cuts the cost of factoring each extra 1024-bit key about 30-fold. Modern 2048-bit keys are unaffected; critics note the 1,600x figure is a theoretical estimate and the measured speed-up was 3.5x.

OfficeChai; DEV Community, 6-7 Nov

Google's TPU output doubles in a quarter

Epoch AI estimates Broadcom shipped nearly 2 million H100-equivalents of TPU compute in May to early August, double the previous quarter, as the newer v7 chip took over; the 2026 figures cover chips for both Google and Anthropic.

Epoch AI, 4 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • SwarmEvolve (Brown University): hundreds of small agents per round reason in hidden vectors instead of text and share their memory caches with a summariser that writes each new program, so evolutionary program search tests 5-13 times more candidates per hour; with a Qwen3 8B model it beat AlphaEvolve's published results on three maths problems (arXiv 2611.08483, high on alphaXiv).
  • Benchmarks as software (Stanford, Christopher Ré): an audit of Terminal-Bench 2.0, a widely used coding-agent benchmark, found defects in about 30 percent of tasks, such as tests that reject valid solutions; the repaired 2.1 raises scores by over 10 points, reshuffles the leaderboard by up to three places, and shows that time limits alone can open or close 20-point gaps between agents (arXiv 2611.08417).
  • Weight-space programming, tested (Shanghai AI Lab): follow-up to last week's result that reasoning models can edit another network's weights directly; editing only 1,023 parameters lifted a small Qwen model 29 points on MATH-500, but gains were much smaller on a 9B model and six of 16 editing attempts found nothing reliable to change (arXiv 2611.09382, Hugging Face papers).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face daily papers, 5-6 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Sunday 8 November 2026
item.description:
The US strikes Iran again while Qatar floats a bridge deal, Stephen Miller becomes Trump's chief of staff, Eisenkot gets the first shot at forming Israel's government, Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv before Tuesday's talks, and OpenAI raises money below its target.

Today's must-read

What Huawei's Horinger data center reveals about China's compute gap (Epoch AI)

Uses satellite images of cooling equipment, substations and generators to estimate one of China's largest AI data centres: about 286 MW and roughly 81,000 H100-equivalents, about 7 percent of SpaceX's Colossus 2 in Tennessee. Explains in real numbers why abundant Chinese power does not close the gap when domestic chips deliver far less compute per watt.

Everyone's talking about

US strikes Iran again; Qatar floats a bridge deal

On Friday night US aircraft hit an air-defence site on Qeshm Island, the first strikes since the midterms; Trump called them 'minor' and said talks are making progress. Iran is studying a reported Qatari plan in which the US would lift its port blockade and free some frozen funds, Iran would admit nuclear inspectors and then reopen Hormuz; Washington has not commented. Oil fell 13 percent on the week, to about 98 dollars a barrel.

Euronews; Times of Israel; &Magazine, 7 Nov

Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as Trump's chief of staff

Trump moved Wiles, his longest-serving chief of staff, to his political operation and named her deputy Miller, the architect of his deportation policy, who starts on Monday. It is the first big shake-up after the midterm defeat; Democrats called Miller an extremist.

ABC (Australia); Axios; Washington Post, 6-7 Nov

Herzog picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu

Israel's president told the former army chief on Saturday that he will get the mandate, formally handed over today, after 67 of 120 lawmakers recommended him. Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14; he rules out Arab-led parties, so he needs both ultra-Orthodox parties for exactly 61 seats or must try a minority government. Netanyahu warned that such a government would 'dismantle the state from within'.

Al Jazeera, 7 Nov

Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv before talks

Overnight into Saturday Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones, mostly at Kyiv and energy sites in 13 regions, damaging a substation that links two nuclear plants to the capital and a Dnipro bridge. Moscow is sending negotiators who stalled earlier rounds to Tuesday's US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, and again rejects any European role or troops in Ukraine.

ISW; &Magazine, 7 Nov

World

Trump asks the Justice Department to investigate Democrats

He accused Democrats who threaten his officials with impeachment of 'extortion', naming Senator Elissa Slotkin and writing that they should be imprisoned. A grand jury earlier declined to indict Slotkin and others over a video on refusing illegal orders.

Fox 2 Detroit, 7 Nov

France's fourth protest weekend

Authorities expected up to 170,000 marchers on Saturday and deployed 70,000 security personnel, banning a Yellow Vests rally near the Élysée. Prime Minister Lecornu meets unions and employers on wages on Monday.

AFP via Daily Sabah, 7 Nov

Sweden

The left side doesn't move

After Friday's shifts by SD and the Centre Party, the Social Democrats said SD's offer changes nothing because a Kristersson government would still depend on SD, and the Left Party said it will not drop its demand for cabinet seats in return for Centre support for Andersson. That makes Andersson's answer to the Centre Party's Friday deadline harder.

SVT, 6 Nov

Russia's 'spy house' on Lidingö is empty

The last Russian occupants have left the seven-storey building, which SVT showed was used by intelligence officers under diplomatic cover; its owner, who bought it at a forced sale in 2014 and never received rent, got inside for the first time this week. The Foreign Ministry defends having protected it under the Vienna Convention.

SVT, this week

Stockholm VC

Funding and firms

  • T-Unit (Daniel Ek, Martin Lorentzon) — AI platform that pulls together information from agencies and companies to help decision-makers in crises — about 50 million euros at a valuation of about 3.5 billion kronor — Lakestar, its first outside investor, plus the founders.
  • Sequoia closes its London office and moves its European investing to California; of its four London partners, one moves to San Francisco, while Luciana Lixandru stays in Europe as a partner after turning down the move.

Swedish Tech News citing Di, 4 Nov; The Next Web; TechCrunch, 4-6 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Sunday 8 November: Herzog formally hands Eisenkot the mandate.
  • Monday 9 November: Miller starts as chief of staff; the House returns, with Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution due Monday or Tuesday; Lecornu meets French unions and employers; G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris (to Tuesday).
  • Tuesday 10 November: Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; US October inflation figures; US-Russia-Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi (to Wednesday); French students and teachers strike.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government presents its budget; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's deadline for M and S to present full government plans, with Kristersson reporting to the Speaker around then; JPMorgan reportedly holds an investor session for Anthropic's planned listing.

&Magazine; SVT; Daily Sabah; FT via Seeking Alpha; earlier editions

Week in review

Voters punished the Iran war, and Washington is reshuffling

Democrats won both chambers on Tuesday, and Republicans blamed the war and fuel prices. Since then a Republican has moved to impeach Hegseth, Wiles has been replaced by Miller, and Trump has paused full-scale strikes while still hitting Iranian targets and talking through Qatar.

AI's money got cheaper

AI stocks had their worst day in 18 months on Thursday, partly on fears that a Democratic Congress will regulate harder, and the sell-off spread to Asia. OpenAI's latest round closed at 1.25 trillion dollars rather than the 1.4 trillion it sought, Anthropic's listing is expected below earlier hopes, and voters and protesters in the US and Europe pushed back against new data centres.

Three democracies, no government

Sweden, Israel and Belgium all spent the week without a working majority. In Sweden SD gave up its claim on cabinet seats and the Centre Party set both blocs a deadline; Israel's opposition won the first chance to govern but lacks 61 seats; Belgium's king refused De Wever's resignation and sent him back to the budget.

Tech and AI

OpenAI raises 11 billion dollars, below its target

The first close of its new round values OpenAI at 1.25 trillion dollars before the new money, with SoftBank and Abu Dhabi's MGX taking part; it reportedly sought over 30 billion at 1.4 trillion. Anthropic is still aiming to list before US Thanksgiving, raising 80-100 billion dollars at 1.25-1.75 trillion, below what investors hoped a month ago, the FT reports.

24/7 Wall St.; The Decoder; FT via Seeking Alpha, 6-7 Nov

Microsoft shuts its AI Frontiers research group

John Langford, a leading machine-learning theorist, announced that the roughly 50-person group behind the AutoGen agent framework is finished and that he is leaving, saying Microsoft AI's leadership favours scaling over research. The post drew one of the weekend's biggest discussions on Hacker News.

hunch.net; HyperAI, 6-7 Nov

Macs quietly map users' families

A researcher's tool shows that macOS has since 2022 built an undocumented on-device knowledge graph from contacts, photos, messages and Family Sharing, with machine-learned guesses about relatives. Apple says the data stays on the device, but it sits in readable database files that any app with full disk access can open.

Eighth Rank via Hacker News; ByteIota, 7 Nov

EU says TikTok's feed breaks the Digital Services Act

In preliminary findings the Commission said the For You feed pulls users into 'rabbit holes' of harmful content and ordered changes, with fines of up to 6 percent of turnover possible; TikTok calls the findings inaccurate.

Al Jazeera; European Commission, 6 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Scientist World (Princeton): agents automatically turned 1,000 recent ML papers into runnable research tasks scored against the reproduced human method; on a ten-task test, frontier models beat it in 84 percent of attempts when improving the method and 74 percent when starting from scratch, and an 8B model trained on the traces with GRPO matched frontier-level ideas (arXiv 2611.08478, top of alphaXiv).
  • Learning dynamics of on-policy distillation (Oxford, EPFL): explains why a student model trained on its own outputs with a teacher's corrections can stall or degrade, and shows that ordinary offline distillation first, even with little immediate gain, makes the later on-policy stage pay off (arXiv 2611.08016).
  • MAC-v2 (UC Berkeley, Sergey Levine): offline reinforcement learning from camera images that plans many steps ahead in a learned world model, made stable by predicting chunks of actions and learning features for control rather than for reconstructing pixels; it beats model-free and model-based baselines on four visual control benchmarks (arXiv 2611.07245).

arXiv via alphaXiv, early November

item.title: Morning Digest, Saturday 7 November 2026
item.description:
The Sweden Democrats drop their demand for cabinet seats and the Centre Party asks both blocs for a full plan, the AI sell-off hits Asia, Belgium's king refuses De Wever's resignation, Israel's opposition lines up behind Eisenkot, and OpenAI releases its first model rated 'Critical' for cyber capability.

Everyone's talking about

The AI sell-off spreads to Asia; Wall Street steadies

On Friday Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each fell about 6 percent and SK Hynix 10 percent after Thursday's US rout. In New York the Nasdaq then rose 1.1 percent and Nvidia nearly 3 percent, though all three main indexes ended the week down. A strong US jobs report (165,000 new jobs against about 59,000 expected; unemployment 4.1 percent) led traders to raise the odds of a December interest-rate rise by the Federal Reserve.

Reuters via Business Standard; Finimize; HNGN, 6-7 Nov

Belgium's king refuses De Wever's resignation

After meeting the five coalition leaders, King Philippe sent the prime minister back to the negotiating table on the 2027 budget, with a report due on 16 November. The parties are split over whether to raise taxes on the wealthiest, and a stopgap monthly budget will probably be needed in January.

Brussels Times; Xinhua, 6 Nov

Israel's opposition backs Eisenkot for prime minister

In consultations with President Herzog, 67 of 120 Knesset members recommended Gadi Eisenkot, including both Arab-led parties and Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu, against 46 for Netanyahu. Herzog names his candidate on Sunday; Netanyahu, who stays on as caretaker, questions the result, while the election committee says the vote was sound.

Sunday Guardian; Haaretz; The Hill, 5-6 Nov

World

Trump's cabinet under strain after the midterms

Republican Thomas Massie says he will force a House vote next week on impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war unless he resigns; several Republicans expect it to pass, and Trump backs Hegseth. Separately, Bloomberg reported that Secretary of State Rubio is weighing leaving; the State Department called it a 'baseless hoax'.

Forbes; Gray News via KGNS; Just Security; Yahoo News, 5-6 Nov

Hackers also tampered with French blood-bank freezers

Attackers took over cold-room controls at a refrigeration supplier to France's blood service, pushing set temperatures to extreme levels at three sites; alarms caught it and no blood products were lost. No one has claimed it, and no link to the recent supermarket freezer attacks has been established.

The Next Web; Newsweek, 4-6 Nov

California empties its death row

Governor Newsom commuted the sentences of all 548 people on death row to life without parole.

Just Security, 6 Nov

Sweden

SD drops its demand for cabinet seats; C asks M and S for a full plan

Jimmie Åkesson said on Friday that the Sweden Democrats will no longer insist on ministers and would accept Kristersson leading a four-party centre-right government without them, setting no counter-demands. The Centre Party replied that it could govern with any party except those on the fringes, and gave Kristersson and Magdalena Andersson until next Friday to present a complete programme with policy, funding and delivery: Kristersson must show how SD would be kept from dictating terms, Andersson how she would govern without the Left Party. Kristersson called both moves welcome, and the Speaker gave him a few more days beyond Tuesday's deadline.

SVT; GP; Morgontidningen, 6 Nov

Border checks extended, now citing Russia

Targeted checks at Sweden's internal Schengen borders will run from 12 November to 11 May. The government now names sabotage and hybrid attacks linked to Russia's war as the reason; May's decision cited crime and terrorism.

Reuters via Internazionale; Xinhua, 5 Nov

Stockholm VC

Funding

  • Sellpy (Michael Arnör) — second-hand clothing platform — about 167 million kronor at a 5.5 billion valuation — H&M (majority owner) and senior staff.
  • Norrsken Evolve — impact investor backing early-stage founders — closes a fund of nearly 700 million kronor, more than planned.

Breakit, this week

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Sunday 8 November: Herzog names who gets the first chance to form Israel's government.
  • 9-10 November: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris.
  • From Monday 9 November: possible House vote on impeaching Hegseth.
  • Tuesday 10 November: Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; US October inflation figures.
  • 10-11 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government presents its budget; Sweden's extended border checks begin; UK third-quarter GDP.
  • Friday 13 November: the Centre Party's deadline for M and S to present their government plans; Kristersson reports to the Speaker around then.

HNGN; Rio Times; Finimize; SVT; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated 'Critical'

The hacking-focused model, the highest risk level in OpenAI's own framework, goes only to vetted customers of its offensive-security programme. OpenAI says it found 81 new high-severity Firefox flaws, now being patched by Mozilla, and solves 48.5 percent of a standard exploit-writing test against 32.1 percent for its predecessor.

Dataconomy; Tech Times, 5-6 Nov

Baidu publishes ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base weights

A 280-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (14 billion active per token) trained on 33.5 trillion tokens, released before any instruction tuning so developers can adapt it; Baidu says it matches DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo V2.5 at similar size, with no independent scores yet.

The Decoder, 5 Nov

Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck

Musk says production in Texas winds down around mid-2027 to free capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi. Sales were about 20,000 last year, against his original forecast of 250,000 a year, and fell another 28 percent this year.

AP via NBC New York, 6 Nov

Google takes over Crusoe's Wyoming data-centre site

A day after announcing a 17-billion-dollar investment in the project, Google bought the site from Crusoe, a company that builds and rents out AI data centres, which had struggled to sign customers for it.

Reuters via TradingView; Bloomberg, 6 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • VFlash (NVIDIA, Johns Hopkins): robot and driving models output plans as boxes and trajectories one coordinate at a time; VFlash predicts each whole shape in one pass, cutting decoding time by about 80 percent while making 3D trajectories more accurate (arXiv 2611.08449, top of both Hugging Face and alphaXiv).
  • Understanding AI from the Inside (Oxford, Mila, EleutherAI and others, with Bengio and Biderman): a book-length survey of mechanistic interpretability that argues the assumption that understanding models' internals makes them safer is largely untested, and calls evaluation standards the field's most pressing gap (arXiv 2611.08438).
  • BestRand (Bosch Research, CMU): scoring a model on a small random slice of a benchmark usually lands close to its full score, but because models fail on similar items an unlucky slice can be far off; drawing many random slices and keeping the one where a few probe models score as they do on the full set halves the risk of large errors across more than 70 benchmarks (arXiv 2611.00883, Hugging Face papers).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face daily papers, 31 Oct-5 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Friday 6 November 2026
item.description:
Wall Street has its worst day for AI stocks in a year and a half, France sees its biggest strike day of the autumn, Trump holds off on Iran, Paraguay's president falls over a bank collapse, and an outside audit says Anthropic's AI is speeding up its own research.

Everyone's talking about

AI stocks crash on Wall Street

The Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent and the Dow 1,833 points (3.4 percent) on Thursday; the chip-stock index lost 12 percent and Nvidia 8.9 percent, its worst day since April 2025, and the market's fear gauge jumped by two-thirds. Triggers cited: a Bloomberg report that Microsoft is stepping back from risky data-centre deals with the rented-capacity providers Nebius, IREN and Nscale (their shares fell 14-17 percent), fears that the new Democratic Congress and states such as Texas will restrict data-centre building, and hedge funds locking in this year's gains. Analysts said company fundamentals had not worsened.

Yahoo Finance; Reuters via Investing.com; CNBC, 5 Nov

France's biggest strike day of the autumn

The interior ministry counted 575,000 marchers nationwide, up from 550,000 on 17 October; unions claimed close to 1.6 million. Police fired tear gas in Lyon, and the government moved next week's G7 foreign ministers' meeting from Marseille to Paris at the last minute.

France 24; Euronews; Reuters via US News, 5 Nov

Trump holds off on restarting the Iran war

Axios reports that Trump leaned towards resuming strikes at Netanyahu's urging but held back after Vance argued for a deal; he says a decision will come soon. Iran sent a new nuclear proposal through Qatar, and the Revolutionary Guard said two tankers and a tug caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, one after hitting a mine (not independently confirmed).

Axios via Fox News; Iran International; HNGN, 5 Nov

Paraguay's president resigns and is impeached minutes later

Santiago Peña quit over his ties to Ueno, a digital bank with about 3 million customers that was seized on Monday and held roughly 800 million dollars of public money, nearly half from state pension and health funds. Congress accepted the resignation, then impeached him unanimously; Vice President Pedro Alliana takes over, and prosecutors seek charges.

AS/COA; NPR, 5 Nov

World

Bank of England raises its rate to 4 percent

It is the first rise in over three years, aimed at inflation driven by fuel prices from the Iran war, and follows the Riksbank's rise on Wednesday.

Euronews, 5 Nov

Trump promises a 'big agreement' after meeting Putin's envoy

Kirill Dmitriev and Ukrainian officials attended a White House event where Melania Trump marked the six-day local ceasefire she brokered in Oleshky, which let nearly 800 people leave. Trump then met Dmitriev alone and said a deal involving more than Ukraine is coming, without details.

AP via KSL, 5 Nov

Russell Brand found guilty

A London jury convicted the comedian of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women between 2005 and 2009.

Euronews, 5 Nov

Sweden

Centre Party leaders meet on the government question

According to SVT and Ekot, C's party board and parliamentary group met on Thursday as Kristersson sounds out a centre-right government that C would let through. C repeats that it will give the Sweden Democrats no influence and will not accept the Left Party in government, and asked the Social Democrats to clarify the Left Party's role. Kristersson reports to the Speaker on Tuesday.

TT via SN; Börsvärlden; SVT, 5 Nov

Supreme Court backs first exclusion order against a gang leader

In its first ruling on the new preventive measure, Högsta domstolen upheld an exclusion order against a man in Biskopsgården whom police describe as a Gothenburg network leader.

SVT Text, 5 Nov

Tighter security ahead of Sweden's Patriot mission in Poland

Polish authorities have raised readiness before the Swedish air-defence unit arrives to guard the NATO hub that ships aid to Ukraine; the deployment is planned to start in December.

SVT, 5 Nov; Government press release, 6 Oct

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Friday 6 November: Belgium's King Philippe decides on Bart De Wever's resignation.
  • 9-10 November: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris.
  • Tuesday 10 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker on his talks; Israel's new Knesset is sworn in; earliest start of Anthropic's investor roadshow.
  • 10-11 November: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.
  • Wednesday 11 November: the Riksbank's new 2 percent rate takes effect.
  • Thursday 12 November: the caretaker government presents its budget.

Italian foreign ministry; Rio Times; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Outside audit: Anthropic's models now improve about twice as fast

METR, given limited inside access, estimates Anthropic's progress on well-specified tasks is about twice its 2024-25 pace (plausibly 1.3 to 3 times) and that roughly 80 percent of the speed-up comes from AI doing research work. Anthropic redacted much of the evidence METR found most informative.

METR, 5 Nov

Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small

Mira Murati's lab's 594-billion-parameter model (17 billion active per token, 1-million-token context) is available through its Tinker platform; the weights are due under the permissive Apache 2.0 licence once outside safety testing is done, possibly next week.

Unite.AI, 5 Nov

AI agents turn an algebraic geometry encyclopedia into checked proofs

Startup Axiom says its agents translated the 7,654-page Stacks Project into about 16 million lines of Lean, a language in which a computer verifies every step; along the way they found dozens of statements that needed missing conditions added, and some that were false. The result is the company's own claim and has not been independently reviewed.

Axiom; TechCrunch, 5 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • FrontierPhysics (Berkeley, Caltech, Stanford and others): 56 end-to-end research tasks built by physicists from their own projects, from literature review to written paper; the best agent, Claude Opus 5.5, passes 27 percent, and expert review blames weak rigour and missing intuition rather than missing physics knowledge (arXiv 2611.06910, top of Hugging Face and alphaXiv).
  • NEO-VLA (NTU, SenseTime): a 2-billion-parameter robot policy with no separate vision encoder, letting the action module read visual features from any layer; it finds the signals useful for control peak in early layers, and it matches or beats the larger pi-0.5 on three real-robot tasks (arXiv 2611.06918).
  • What multi-turn RL really improves (Chinese Academy of Sciences): RL-trained agents do not make better individual moves but recover from errors better, so their edge shrinks or reverses when the number of allowed steps is tight; training with varied step budgets recovers 4-5 points (arXiv 2611.06483).

arXiv via alphaXiv; Hugging Face daily papers, 4 Nov
